product_overview: A small Next.js demo application that showcases authentication (hardcoded test credentials), a protected dashboard, a client-side validated contact form with an API endpoint, site navigation, and a custom 404 page. The original PRD (see pages 1-7 of the provided document) documents hardcoded credentials (test@example.com / password123) and cookie-based auth (auth-token=logged-in).
core_goals: Authenticate using test credentials and access a protected dashboard
Submit a contact inquiry using a client-validated form and receive a success confirmation
Navigate the site between Home, About, Contact, Login and Dashboard pages
Retrieve a simple API hello message from the /api/hello endpoint
Handle invalid routes with a user-friendly 404 page

features.name: User Login
features.description: Allow a user to sign in with the demo credentials so they can access protected content.
user_flows: Navigate to /login -> Fill email input field with test@example.com -> Fill password input field with password123 -> Submit login form -> Be redirected to /dashboard and see the dashboard content

Navigate to /login -> Fill email input field with wrong@example.com -> Fill password input field with wrongpass -> Submit login form -> Stay on /login and see error message "Use test@example.com / password123"

features.name: Protected Dashboard
features.description: Show protected content only to authenticated users and provide a logout action that clears authentication.
user_flows: Navigate to /login -> Fill email input field with test@example.com -> Fill password input field with password123 -> Submit login form -> Be redirected to /dashboard and see welcome message "Welcome! You are logged in."
Directly navigate to /dashboard without authenticating -> Be redirected to /login
While on /dashboard as an authenticated user -> Trigger logout action -> Be redirected to /login and no longer see dashboard content

features.name: Contact Form
features.description: Collect name, email and message from users with client-side validation and send the submission to the /api/contact endpoint.
user_flows: Navigate to /contact -> Fill name input field -> Fill email input field -> Fill message textarea -> Submit form -> See success message "Message sent!" (green)
Navigate to /contact -> Leave one or more required fields empty or invalid -> Submit form -> See error message "Fill all fields correctly." (red)

features.name: Navigation
features.description: Provide a consistent top navigation bar across the site so users can move between primary pages.
user_flows: Navigate to / -> Observe navigation bar with links to Home, About, Contact, Login, Dashboard -> Use navigation to go to /about -> Observe About page content -> Use navigation to go to /contact -> Observe Contact page content -> Use navigation to go to /login -> Observe Login page

features.name: API Hello Endpoint
features.description: Expose a simple GET API that returns a static hello message for testing API connectivity.
user_flows: Navigate to /api/hello -> Observe JSON response with message "Hello from TestSprite API!"

features.name: Home Page
features.description: Landing page introducing the demo and listing testable features.
user_flows: Navigate to / -> See heading "Welcome to TestSprite Demo" -> See a paragraph describing the app purpose -> See a bullet list that includes Authentication flows, Form validation and submission, API routes, Protected pages, Navigation and routing

features.name: About Page
features.description: Static informational page describing the demo features and purpose.
user_flows: Navigate to /about -> See heading "About This Demo" -> See a list describing features such as login with test credentials and the protected dashboard

features.name: Custom 404 Page
features.description: Display a friendly 404 page for invalid routes and provide a way to return home.
user_flows: Navigate to /_not-found -> See heading "404 - Page Not Found" -> See subtitle "The page you are looking for does not exist." -> Use the "Go Home" link to return to /

known_limitations.issue: Authentication uses client-side cookie check only, not server-side validation
known_limitations.impact: Auth state is managed entirely in browser, no server-side protection

known_limitations.impact: Only test@example.com/password123 works, no user management
